text.p: The following is a factfile on Gustavo Kuerten, winner of the French Open on Sunday:
Aged eight: Started playing tennis with older brother Rafael, who is now a tennis teacher in their hometown.
Aged 14: Decided between playing soccer or competitive tennis.
Aged 17: Finished season as one of the world's top ranked juniors, number six in singles. Won French Open junior doubles title.

Perhaps the biggest surprise at a French Open littered with upsets and the unexpected. Had never won an ATP tournament and recorded only one victory in his two previous Grand Slam appearances. Survived three five-set tests and a four-set semifinal on his way to becoming the first Brazilian man to reach and then win a Grand Slam title, revealing great agility, stamina and coolness in tight situations. First gained attention at Roland Garros with his colourful attire, although officials have pleaded with him to wear more traditional whites rather than his yellow and blue kit.
Seeding: unseeded. Age: 20. Plays right-handed. Weight: 82 kg. Height: 1.90m. Ranking: 66. Tournament wins: 0. Career prize money: $980,278 (including $695,500 for winning the French Open).
